column1: # One row per policy line a resolver pack advertises to every caller that reads
# The census enumerates the lines from their PRODUCERS (the Rust literals in
# rows in `migrations/`) and refuses any line this file does not cover. A pack
# added to either producer fails the gate until its six lines are adjudicated.
# 🔴 THE VALUE IS PART OF THE ROW BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION OF THIS FILE LEFT
# IT OUT. Keyed by pack and field alone, a verdict outlived the line that
# earned it: flipping R3's `subresource_policy` from `deny` to `allow` in the
# producer left the census GREEN, still reporting `enforced — .7.3.5` for a
# line advertising the opposite of what that leaf repaired. Measured in situ,
# then restored byte-identical. A judgement about a word is gated on the word.
# ⭐ WHY THIS FILE IS SEPARATE FROM THE CENSUS. A verdict is a judgement with
# evidence behind it; an enumeration is a command. Keeping them apart is what
# lets the census be re-run against a tree whose verdicts have changed — and it
# is why `--check` can be a gate at all. The census never grades; this file
# The vocabulary (`VERDICTS` in the census, which refuses anything else):
#   enforced      a mechanism refuses AND a control has been observed RED; the
#                 evidence column names the leaf or commit that observed it.
#   unverified    a mechanism is present and covered, but no RED is on record.
#                 ⛔ NOT a defect and NOT a weaker `enforced` — it is the named
#                 gap `docs/CLAIM_VERIFICATION.md` §4 asks for rather than a
#                 hidden one. The line rests on READING the mechanism.
#   vacuous       the pack has no mechanism that could violate the line; the
#                 evidence names what establishes the absence. ⚠️ Nothing would
#                 notice if it stopped being vacuous.
#   unenforced    the pack can violate the line and nothing refuses. A defect.
#   undefined     the advertised word has no stated meaning anywhere in the
#                 repository, so the line is neither true nor false as written.
#   misdescribed  the word names something other than what the code does; the
#                 ADVERTISEMENT is what is wrong, not the code.
#   open          measured, routed to a named sibling leaf, not yet adjudicated.
# ⛔ `vacuous` IS NOT `enforced`, and collapsing them is the mistake this file
# exists to prevent. R0 advertises `javascript_policy: "deny"` and runs no
# script engine — true today, guarded by nothing, and silently false the day R0
# gains one. `SIGNOFF-REPAIR.7.3.5` repaired two lines that had been vacuous
# right up until the pack they described started executing pages.
# ── r0-https-fetcher — in-process HTTPS acquisition; the bytes go to storage ──

DEFINED by .7.3.6.5 from ROADMAP.md §16's `archive-depth` policy: `deny` = the pack does not expand an archive NESTED inside the container it acquired. R0 expands nothing at all — the bytes go to storage

column6: ⚠️ VERDICT CORRECTED by .7.3.6.5, from `misdescribed`. REPAIR-0266 judged the in-product code path — the pack performs no egress — and that was the wrong granularity. The class is the MAXIMUM of the ACQUISITION the pack delivers, and an enrolled agent's reach is genuinely unbounded, so `any` is the honest ceiling. Nothing can violate `any`, hence vacuous. ⭐ .7.3.6.4 gives it teeth: a caller must now permit `any` to be served this pack
`none` claims no isolation, and the pack runs nothing to isolate
no dial is performed, so no hop exists to follow or refuse
the pack opens nothing
no document is fetched or parsed
nothing is executed in-product
